analysis: The PR changes one documentation file, docs/architecture/inference.md, adding a single troubleshooting table row at head line 2371. The row says a cold load can be refused with the ordinary slot 503 or insufficient-memory error while an idle model is resident, because that slot holds an unexpired Autopilot placement hold. It names ProviderLoop.evictableModelSlots, autopilotHoldsModel, autopilotHeldWeightBytes and ProviderLoop+AutopilotPlacement.swift. The supplied base text (lines 1-802) is the surrounding Nemotron Super and GLM material and does not contain the changed hunk. No executable code, authorization, attestation, encryption, or key handling is modified. The row documents an availability behavior: Autopilot holds exclude a slot from eviction and deny it a free_for_load_gb reclaim credit. The text does not show who can create or extend a hold, which is outside the supplied evidence. If the hold source is coordinator-controlled, TB-002 trusts the coordinator, so this is not a new attack surface. If a consumer or provider can influence holds, that is a DoS question (related to T-029, T-057) for the Autopilot source and model-autopilot.md. Those files are not supplied, so I cannot confirm hold expiry or authorization. The base text I examined, including Nemotron prefix-cache and bank descriptions that touch T-041, is unchanged. The cache scope partitioning described there (authenticated tenant scope, no scope means cold) matches the T-041 mitigations. No threat-model assumption is invalidated by the docs change. The next pass should check ProviderLoop+AutopilotPlacement.swift for hold authority, bounded TTL and expiry.
